question: we're up on the ridge and just heard thunder, what do we do
keyPoints: Get off the ridge and summit right away, down to lower ground
Avoid lone tall trees, open ground and water; don't wait for the storm to arrive
Spread the group out
redFlags: Shelter under a lone tall tree
Stay on the ridge to wait it out

question: there's six of us caught out in a thunderstorm, should we huddle together
keyPoints: No: spread out (at least about 50 feet apart) so one strike can't hit everyone

question: is our tent a safe place to wait out lightning
keyPoints: No: a tent gives no protection from lightning
There is no safe place outdoors; reduce risk by getting off high ground, away from tall isolated objects

question: the thunder stopped, how long before we keep hiking up
keyPoints: Wait at least 30 minutes after the last thunder before going back out or up

question: how can i tell how close the lightning is
keyPoints: Count seconds from the flash to the thunder: about 5 seconds per mile
If you can hear thunder, you are close enough to be struck

question: we're climbing a peak tomorrow, how do we avoid getting caught by lightning
keyPoints: Start early and be off summits and ridges before afternoon storms build
Watch the sky for building clouds and turn back at the first thunder

question: my buddy just got struck by lightning, is it safe to touch him
keyPoints: Yes: a person struck by lightning carries no charge and is safe to touch
Check breathing and start CPR if needed; get help

question: we want to hike the slot canyon but there are clouds over the mountains
keyPoints: Rain miles away can send a flash flood through the canyon: don't go in if storms are possible anywhere upstream
Know the escape routes to high ground
redFlags: Says it is fine if it isn't raining where you are

question: the creek in the canyon suddenly got muddy and there's a roaring sound
keyPoints: Signs of a flash flood: climb to high ground immediately
Don't try to outrun it down the canyon

question: is it ok to camp in the dry wash, it's nice and flat
keyPoints: No: dry washes and streambeds can flood fast with no warning; camp on higher ground

question: there's water running over the dirt road to the trailhead, can we drive through
keyPoints: No: turn around, don't drown; a little moving water can float a car
Wait or find another way

question: the water is rising around us in the canyon and we can't get out
keyPoints: Climb as high as you can: a ledge, rocks, the canyon wall
Stay out of the water and wait for it to drop

question: the river rose overnight and now we can't cross back to the trailhead
keyPoints: Don't cross high or fast water; wait for the level to drop (often lower in the early morning)
Look for a safer crossing or another route

question: what do i do if i get swept off my feet crossing a stream
keyPoints: Float on your back, feet first and pointed downstream
Don't stand up in fast water (feet can get trapped); work toward shore at an angle

question: we can see a column of smoke over the next ridge
keyPoints: Leave the area: head away from the fire, downhill and upwind if you can
Don't wait to see if it grows

question: the wildfire is coming toward us and we can't outrun it
keyPoints: Get to an area with little fuel: a rock field, a road, a stream, an already burned area
Lie face down, cover skin, shield yourself from heat; breathe the cooler air near the ground
redFlags: Says to run uphill ahead of the fire

question: the smoke is so thick it's hard to breathe
keyPoints: Move away from the smoke to lower ground or cleaner air
Cover nose and mouth; get help if breathing trouble gets worse

question: it's really windy and dry, is it ok to have a small campfire
keyPoints: No: in high winds and dry conditions, don't build a fire; follow fire restrictions

question: how do we make sure our campfire is really out
keyPoints: Drown it with water, stir the ashes, drown again
Feel for heat; it must be cold to the touch before you leave

question: we're stuck on a ledge and can't climb up or down
keyPoints: Stop: don't try a risky move; stay put and make yourselves secure
Signal for help (whistle, light, bright clothing) and stay warm while you wait
redFlags: Says to try to climb down anyway

question: the trail ended at a cliff and we're not sure how we got here
keyPoints: Stop and don't try to down-climb unknown terrain
Go back the way you came if it's safe; if lost, stay put and signal

question: a storm rolled in and we can barely see in the snow
keyPoints: Stop moving if you can't see the route; shelter from the wind and stay together
Stay warm and dry, wait for visibility
